(i) the tensor of curvature is a well defined object at any point on a smooth surface, (ii) it can be estimated by computing in closed-form the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of 3 3 matrices that can be computed from a polyhedaral approximation of the surface, (iii) the resulting algorithm is linear both in time and space as a function of number of vertices and number of faces of the polyhedron.

the principal curvatures of a surface at a point p can be computed by integrating the principal curvaturse of the surface in a 3 3 matrix over a small sphere centered at p, and that the principal directions can be computed by taking the eigenvalues of the integral.

the tensor of curvature at a point of a surface is the average, with respect to the Gaussian measure, of the tensor of the surface in the neighborhood of that point, and that the tensor of a surface in a neighborhood can be estimated by the tensor of the polyhedgeon at the vertex of the polyhederal approximation closest to that neighborhood.
